title: Addressing Teeth Crowding in Children: Causes and Treatment
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Teeth crowding happens when there isn't enough room in a child's mouth for teeth to come in straight, often from genetics or losing baby teeth too early. Catching it early lets a dentist guide jaw growth and plan treatment before it becomes a bigger problem.
content: Teeth crowding in children happens when there isn't enough space in the mouth for teeth to come in straight, leading to overlapping, twisted, or misaligned teeth. It's often caused by genetics, losing baby teeth too early, or a mismatch between jaw size and tooth size. Catching it early makes a real difference in how it's managed. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, care for teeth crowding starts with a full dental checkup that looks at how the teeth and jaw are developing. This lets the dentist spot problems while there's still time to guide growth, rather than waiting until all the permanent teeth have come in. Treatment depends on the child's age and how severe the crowding is. Options range from preventive care and holding space for permanent teeth to early orthodontic guidance that helps teeth come in with enough room. Regular checkups along the way help track whether the jaw and teeth are developing as expected. Parents in Kolkata who notice crowded or overlapping teeth in their child should book a consultation sooner rather than later. Early action tends to mean simpler treatment and better long-term results.

title: Understanding Overbite and Crossbite in Children's Dental Health
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: An overbite means the upper teeth overlap the lower teeth more than they should. A crossbite means some upper teeth sit inside the lower teeth instead of outside. Both can affect chewing and speech if left unchecked, which is why routine dental visits matter for catching them early.
content: An overbite is when the upper front teeth overlap the lower teeth more than normal. A crossbite is when one or more upper teeth sit inside the lower teeth instead of outside, the reverse of a normal bite. Both can affect how a child chews, speaks, and how their jaw develops if they aren't addressed. These bite issues are usually picked up during a child's routine dental checkup. Spotting them early gives the dentist time to plan corrective care while the jaw is still growing, which is when treatment tends to work best. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, children are checked for bite and alignment problems as a standard part of their dental visits. If a child is chewing awkwardly, has visibly uneven teeth, or seems to have jaw discomfort, it's worth getting it looked at rather than waiting. Early evaluation gives parents a clearer picture of what, if anything, needs to be done, and keeps small issues from turning into bigger ones later.

title: Pediatric Dentist vs. General Dentist: Choosing the Right Care
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: A pediatric dentist trains specifically in children's dental care, from growth and development to preventive treatment. A general dentist treats patients of all ages, covering everything from checkups to fillings. Both matter for oral health, but which one a family needs depends on the child's age and the issue at hand.
content: Knowing the difference between a pediatric dentist and a general dentist helps you pick the right person for the job. A pediatric dentist trains specifically to treat children, focusing on how their teeth and jaws grow, preventive care, and putting young patients at ease. A general dentist treats patients of all ages and handles routine checkups, fillings, cleanings, and basic restorative work. Both types of dentist play a real role in oral health. Pediatric dentists usually have more training in managing children's behavior in the chair and spotting developmental problems early. General dentists can and do treat children too, depending on the case and how comfortable the child is. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, our dentists treat both children and adults. A dental checkup helps decide the right approach based on age, the condition of the teeth, and what the patient actually needs. Seeing a dentist regularly, whichever kind, catches problems before they become bigger ones. If you're not sure whether your child needs a pediatric dentist or whether a general dentist will do, ask us and we'll point you in the right direction.

title: The Importance of Specialized Pediatric Dentists for Early Care
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: A child's early experiences at the dentist shape how they feel about oral health for years to come. Pediatric dentists focus on tracking jaw growth, catching cavities early, and handling developmental milestones in a way that keeps kids calm rather than anxious. That groundwork matters for how permanent teeth come in, how speech develops, and how a child chews.
content: A child's first dental visits shape how they feel about going to the dentist for years afterward. Pediatric dentists look after more than just cleanings, they pay attention to how a young mouth is growing and behaving. Baby teeth and developing jaws need their own kind of attention, since they set up how permanent teeth will come in, how speech develops, and how a child learns to chew properly. This kind of care means tracking growth patterns, catching early childhood cavities before they spread, and handling developmental milestones in a calm, reassuring way. Done well, it turns what could be a stressful visit into a routine part of a child's life, rather than something to dread. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, we try to make dental visits approachable from a child's very first appointment, whether they're a toddler or a teenager. Getting a child comfortable with the dentist early is one of the better things a parent can do for their long-term dental health. If you're weighing why pediatric-focused care matters, our team can walk you through what to expect and how we handle young patients.

title: Affordable Dental Implants: Restoring Function and Aesthetics
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Dental implants give artificial teeth a stable base, improving both comfort and how the bite lines up. Whether someone is a good candidate depends on their oral health, bone support, and medical history. Knowing the process, the stages involved, and what upkeep is needed afterward makes for a smoother decision. Good hygiene and follow-up visits keep an implant working well.
content: Dental implants are a common way to replace missing teeth and get back normal chewing and speech. They work by giving an artificial tooth a stable base, which helps with both comfort and how the teeth line up. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, anyone considering implants gets a full checkup before any treatment is planned. That means looking at gum health, jaw bone support, and general medical history, since all of these affect whether implants are a good option and how well they'll hold up. A proper consultation walks the patient through what the process actually involves: the stages of treatment, healing time, and what maintenance looks like afterward, so there aren't surprises along the way. Good oral hygiene and regular follow-up visits matter just as much after the implant is placed as the surgery itself. Anyone in Kolkata weighing dental implants should talk through the options with a dentist first. A clear-eyed consultation makes it easier to know whether implants are the right fit and what to expect going forward.

title: Cosmetic Veneers: Enhancing Your Smile with Custom Shells
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Cosmetic veneers are thin, custom-made shells fitted to the front of teeth to fix chips, discoloration, or gaps. Whether they're right for someone depends on a proper dental evaluation. The process takes planning and a close look at the health of the teeth first. Alternatives may suit some patients better, depending on enamel and bite. Talking it through with an experienced dentist helps in choosing what actually fits.
content: Cosmetic veneers are thin, custom-made shells fitted over the front of teeth to improve how a smile looks. They're commonly used for teeth that are chipped, discolored, uneven, or slightly out of alignment, reshaping and recoloring them to look more natural and even. Whether veneers are the right choice depends on the individual, their oral health, and what they're hoping to achieve. A proper evaluation by a dentist is needed to check suitability and make sure the results will hold up over time. Getting veneers done well takes careful planning and close attention to the underlying health of the teeth, not just how they'll look afterward. In some cases, a dentist may suggest a different treatment altogether, depending on the condition of the enamel, how the bite lines up, and the overall structure of the teeth. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, patients get a detailed consultation and smile assessment before any veneer work is planned, so the diagnosis and treatment plan actually fit the case. Talking to an experienced dentist first makes it easier to know whether veneers are the right route, or whether something else would serve better.

title: Safe and Effective Teeth Whitening Options for a Brighter Smile
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Professional teeth whitening comes in a few forms, from in-clinic treatments to dentist-supervised home kits. A dental checkup beforehand helps confirm what's actually safe for a given patient's teeth and gums. Simple habits afterward help the results last. The right method comes down to enamel condition and what the patient wants to achieve. A qualified dentist should be involved before starting any whitening treatment.
content: Teeth whitening is a common choice for people looking to lighten stained or discolored teeth. The right method depends on the person's oral health, enamel condition, and what they're hoping to achieve, and it should be guided by a dentist rather than done blind. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, patients are walked through the whitening options that suit them after a proper checkup. That can mean in-clinic whitening, a dentist-supervised take-home kit, polishing to remove surface stains, or a broader cosmetic plan if whitening is only part of what's needed. Sometimes the advice is simpler: a cleaning and some maintenance habits to keep results looking good. A checkup before starting any whitening treatment matters, since it confirms the method is actually safe for that patient's teeth and gums, not just effective. Anyone considering whitening should talk to a dentist first rather than reaching for an over-the-counter kit, both for safety and for a result that actually lasts.

title: Composite and Cosmetic Dental Fillings: Restoring Teeth Naturally
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Composite fillings are tooth-colored and blend in naturally, which is why they're often used in spots that show when you smile. The right filling depends on the size of the cavity, where the tooth sits, and how much bite pressure it takes. Keeping up with hygiene and checkups matters for how long a filling lasts. A dental exam is what actually determines the best option.
content: Fillings are the standard fix for cavities and minor tooth damage. Composite fillings are tooth-colored and blend in with the surrounding teeth, which makes them a common choice for spots that show when someone smiles. They hold up well and look natural, which is part of why they've become the go-to option in a lot of cases. Other cosmetic filling materials aim for the same balance of looks and strength, and which one makes sense depends on where the tooth is and what it needs to withstand. The size of the cavity, the tooth's location, how much bite pressure it takes, and the patient's overall oral health all factor into the decision, which is why a proper dental exam comes before any filling is chosen. Keeping up with brushing, flossing, and regular checkups matters for how long any filling lasts and whether new decay shows up nearby. In Kolkata, more patients are asking about these restorative options as awareness of what's available grows. Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic offers consultations for composite and other cosmetic fillings, with the exam and treatment choice built around what each tooth actually needs.

title: Teeth Whitening: A Popular Cosmetic Dentistry Trend
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Teeth whitening remains one of the most requested cosmetic dental treatments, valued for how much it can brighten a smile. Doing it under a dentist's supervision keeps the process safe and limits sensitivity. Simple maintenance habits afterward help the results stick. Modern dental care in Kolkata has made these treatments easier to access. A qualified dentist can guide patients toward the safest, most effective option for their teeth.
content: Cosmetic dentistry has grown more popular as people pay more attention to how their smile looks. Teeth whitening is one of the most requested treatments, since it's a straightforward way to deal with stains from food, drinks, smoking, and ordinary aging. The appeal is obvious: it's a simple, non-invasive procedure with a visible result. Done under a dentist's supervision, whitening is safer and more even than store-bought kits, and it tends to cause less sensitivity afterward. Along with the whitening itself, a dentist may suggest some maintenance habits to help the results last longer. Access to this kind of cosmetic care has improved in Kolkata in recent years. Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic offers consultations for teeth whitening and other cosmetic treatments, starting with an oral health checkup to make sure the plan actually fits the patient. Choosing a qualified dentist for whitening means getting a method suited to your teeth, rather than a one-size-fits-all approach, while keeping the rest of your mouth healthy too.

title: The Growing Demand for Professional Teeth Whitening
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Teeth whitening is popular because it is quick, non-invasive, and gives visible results. Lifestyle habits and social situations have pushed demand higher. More patients now choose supervised treatment over unverified over-the-counter kits. This reflects a preference for safety and results that last. A dentist assesses each case before recommending an approach.
content:
Teeth whitening has become one of the most requested treatments in cosmetic dentistry because it improves how a smile looks without surgery or major dental work. Growing awareness of oral aesthetics, along with everyday habits like tea, coffee, and tobacco use that stain teeth, has driven more people to ask about it. Social and professional situations also play a part, since people want their smile to look its best for photos, interviews, or public-facing roles.

More patients are now choosing supervised whitening over unverified over-the-counter kits, largely because a dentist can check enamel condition first and use a concentration and method suited to that patient rather than a one-size-fits-all product. This shift reflects a general move toward safety and predictable, longer-lasting results.

Before starting treatment, a dentist examines the teeth and gums, checks for existing sensitivity or decay, and recommends the whitening method suited to the case. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Newtown, Kolkata, this assessment comes first, followed by a clear explanation of what the treatment can and can't achieve so patients know what to expect before they commit to it.

title: Safe Teeth Whitening Options for Sensitive Teeth
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: People with sensitive teeth need extra planning before whitening to avoid discomfort. A dental check first identifies what's causing the sensitivity. Dentists often use milder agents or supervised procedures to keep the process comfortable. Good oral hygiene and avoiding very hot or cold food during treatment also help. Getting this right takes a proper evaluation, not guesswork.
content:
Whitening sensitive teeth safely takes more planning than a standard whitening treatment. Some people feel sharp discomfort with certain whitening methods, so it helps to get a dental opinion before starting anything.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, the first step is usually a check of what's actually causing the sensitivity, whether that's enamel wear, gum irritation, or an existing cavity that needs treating first. Once that's clear, the dentist can plan around it.

For sensitive teeth, whitening is often done under direct supervision using a milder bleaching agent, applied for shorter sessions to limit discomfort. This usually means the whitening happens more gradually, but with less risk of pain during or after the sessions.

Simple habits help too: keeping up regular brushing and flossing, and avoiding very hot or cold food and drink for a day or two after each session. Because every mouth reacts differently, the plan gets adjusted patient by patient rather than following a fixed protocol.

title: Factors Affecting the Cost of Teeth Whitening
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: What you pay for teeth whitening depends on the method used, how stained the teeth already are, and the dentist's experience. In-clinic and take-home kits differ in technique, time, and results. Some cases need extra cleaning or prep work first. The right option really comes down to an individual check-up, not a fixed price list.
content:
Teeth whitening is one of the most common cosmetic treatments people ask about, but the price varies quite a bit from patient to patient depending on a few clinical factors.

The method matters most: an in-clinic procedure uses stronger agents under direct supervision and gives faster results in one or two sittings, while a take-home kit works more gradually over one to two weeks at a lower cost. How stained or discoloured the teeth already are also affects the plan. Heavier staining, from years of tea, coffee, or tobacco use, may need more sessions or a combined approach.

In some cases, a dentist will recommend a professional cleaning or treat an existing cavity before whitening begins, since untreated issues can affect both comfort and results. The dentist's experience and the quality of the whitening material used also factor into the overall cost.

Because no two mouths are the same, Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata starts with an examination before quoting a price or recommending a method. That way, the plan fits the actual condition of the teeth rather than a standard package.

title: Laser Teeth Whitening: Pros, Cons, and What to Expect
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Laser teeth whitening uses a light-activated gel to lift stains faster than standard methods, done under a dentist's supervision. It can noticeably brighten teeth in a single sitting, though some patients feel temporary sensitivity afterward. How well it works depends on enamel condition and habits like tea, coffee, or tobacco use. An oral exam beforehand confirms whether it's the right fit.
content:
Laser teeth whitening speeds up a standard whitening treatment by using a light source to activate the bleaching gel, which shortens the time needed to see a visible change in tooth shade. In Kolkata, patients often ask about it for staining caused by tea, coffee, tobacco use, ageing, or certain diets.

The procedure is done in-clinic, and only after a dentist has examined the teeth and gums to confirm there's nothing else that needs treating first, such as a cavity or gum inflammation.

The main advantage is speed: most patients see a noticeably brighter shade in a single session. The trade-off is that some people experience temporary sensitivity to hot or cold for a day or two afterward, and the degree of improvement still depends on the natural condition of the enamel and habits like smoking or frequent coffee drinking, which can cause new staining over time.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, patients get a clear rundown of what laser whitening can realistically achieve, including the temporary discomfort some people feel, before deciding whether to go ahead.

title: Managing Tooth Sensitivity After Whitening Procedures
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Feeling sensitive to hot or cold after a whitening session is common and usually fades on its own. Desensitizing toothpaste and skipping extreme temperatures for a day or two help manage it. It happens because the whitening agent temporarily affects the enamel or exposes the dentin underneath. If it doesn't settle down, it's worth getting checked.
content:
Some sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet food after a whitening session is common and normally goes away within a few days. It happens as the teeth adjust to the bleaching agent used during treatment.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, this is checked for during the initial exam. Patients are looked at first to confirm whitening is a safe option for their teeth and gums before treatment starts, which helps limit how much sensitivity shows up afterward.

The discomfort usually comes from temporary changes in the enamel surface or from small areas of exposed dentin underneath. To manage it, a desensitizing toothpaste, avoiding very hot or cold food and drink for a short period, and sticking to normal brushing and flossing are usually enough.

If sensitivity doesn't ease off after a few days or gets worse, it's worth going back to the dentist. That kind of follow-up rules out anything else going on, like an untreated cavity or gum issue, and gets the discomfort dealt with properly rather than just waiting it out.

title: Debunking Common Myths About Teeth Whitening
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Professional teeth whitening does not damage enamel when it's done properly, despite what many people assume. The results aren't permanent either, since diet, hygiene, and habits like smoking affect how long they last. Over-the-counter kits also aren't a like-for-like substitute for professional treatment. Knowing the facts helps patients choose the right option.
content:
A few myths keep coming up around teeth whitening, and they often steer people toward decisions that don't actually serve them well.

The first is that whitening damages enamel. Done under professional supervision, it doesn't: the procedure is designed to work on the tooth surface without harming its structure. The second is that results last forever. They don't. How long a whitened smile stays bright depends on diet, brushing habits, and things like tea, coffee, or tobacco use, all of which can bring staining back over months or years.

A third myth is that over-the-counter whitening strips or gels work just as well as professional treatment. They can help a little, but the concentration is weaker and less consistent, and there's no dentist checking the teeth beforehand, so results and safety both suffer by comparison.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, walking patients through what whitening can and can't do is part of the first visit, so the decision to go ahead, or not, is based on facts rather than assumptions. A dental check beforehand also means the treatment gets matched to the actual condition of the teeth.

title: Maxillofacial Expertise for Complex Dental Issues
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Jaw pain, impacted teeth, facial injuries, and oral infections often need more than routine dental care. A maxillofacial specialist is trained to handle the teeth, jaw, and facial structures together rather than treating them separately. Getting the right specialist early tends to mean a smoother recovery and fewer complications. Persistent jaw pain or dental discomfort is worth having checked properly.
content:
Some dental problems go beyond a routine filling or cleaning. Jaw pain, impacted teeth, facial injuries, and oral infections often need a maxillofacial specialist, someone trained to diagnose and treat conditions across the teeth, jaw, and facial bones rather than just one area at a time.

Bringing in a dentist with this training from the start means the treatment plan accounts for both the dental side and, where needed, the surgical side of a problem, instead of switching between specialists partway through. In practice, that usually means a clearer diagnosis and a smoother recovery.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, complex cases get a proper work-up before any treatment starts, looking at what's actually causing the pain or injury rather than just addressing the symptom in front of them. If jaw pain or dental discomfort has been sticking around, or if a case looks like it needs more than a standard procedure, seeing a maxillofacial specialist early usually heads off bigger problems down the line.

title: When to See a Prosthodontist for Restorative Dental Care
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: A prosthodontist handles restoring or replacing teeth, from crowns and bridges to dentures and implants. It's worth seeing one for missing teeth, trouble chewing, worn-down teeth, or a smile you'd like to improve. Going in early usually means simpler treatment and a better result. A proper consultation lays out which restorative option actually fits the case.
content:
A prosthodontist deals with restoring or replacing teeth so a patient can chew, speak, and smile normally again. That covers crowns, bridges, dentures, dental implants, and, in more involved cases, full-mouth rehabilitation.

It's worth booking a consultation if there are missing teeth, ongoing difficulty chewing, teeth that are visibly worn down or damaged, or simply a smile that isn't working the way the patient wants. Going in sooner rather than later usually keeps the treatment simpler and avoids problems building up over time, like shifting teeth or bite changes from a gap that's been left too long.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, prosthodontic treatment starts with a plan built around what the patient actually needs, along with a straightforward explanation of the options, the aftercare involved, and what a realistic result looks like before any work begins.

title: Endodontic Surgery vs. Laser Endodontics for Deep Infections
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Endodontic surgery usually comes in when a standard root canal isn't enough to clear a deep infection. Laser endodontics instead uses light-based technology to clean and disinfect the canal more precisely. Which one fits depends on how complex the infection is. Either way, catching it early and keeping up with checkups matters more than the choice of technique.
content:
Deep tooth infections that don't respond to a standard root canal usually get treated one of two ways: endodontic surgery or laser endodontics. Surgery is typically the option when a conventional root canal has already been tried and hasn't fully cleared the infection. Laser endodontics instead uses light-based technology during the procedure to clean and disinfect the canal more thoroughly than manual instruments alone.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, the choice between them comes down to how the infection looks on examination and imaging, not a default preference for one method. Laser treatment tends to be more precise and, for many patients, more comfortable during the procedure, while surgery remains the better fit for more complicated or long-standing infections.

Either way, a proper evaluation beforehand is what actually determines whether the infection clears and stays cleared. Keeping up with brushing, flossing, and regular checkups afterward lowers the odds of needing this kind of treatment again.

title: Reconstructive Dental Surgery After Tumor Removal
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Reconstructive surgery after tumor removal restores how the mouth functions and looks. Careful planning between the surgical and reconstructive team, and steady follow-up care afterward, is what determines how well a patient recovers.
content: Reconstructive surgery after tumor removal rebuilds the tissue and structure needed to eat, speak, and look the same as before. Getting good results starts well before the reconstruction itself, since the surgical team plans out what will be removed and how it will be rebuilt ahead of the original tumor surgery. Recovery is a gradual process, with follow-up visits to check healing and adjust as needed rather than one single fix. Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata works with patients through each stage of this process, explaining what to expect and answering questions along the way so patients know what's ahead before treatment begins.

title: Space Maintainers for Healthy Dental Development in Children
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: A space maintainer holds open the gap left when a child loses a baby tooth too early, so the permanent tooth coming in later has room to grow in straight. Left alone, that gap can close as neighboring teeth drift, leading to crowding down the line.
content: When a child loses a baby tooth well before its permanent replacement is ready, whether from decay, injury, or early extraction, a space maintainer is often fitted to hold that gap open. Without it, neighboring teeth can drift into the empty space, leaving too little room for the adult tooth to come in straight. Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata fits children with a space maintainer suited to which tooth was lost and how long until the permanent tooth is due, and checks progress at follow-up visits before removing the device once it's no longer needed.

title: Pediatric Oral Hygiene: Building Healthy Habits Early
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Brushing, flossing, and diet habits formed in childhood are what prevent most cavities and gum problems later on. Regular dental visits catch decay or bite issues early, while good habits at home build a foundation kids carry into adulthood.
content: Good oral hygiene habits formed early in childhood do most of the work in preventing cavities, gum problems, and bigger dental issues later on. Brushing twice a day, flossing once teeth are close together, and limiting sugary snacks and drinks are the basics that matter most. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, children get age-appropriate care in a calm setting, with dentists showing kids and parents the right brushing technique and keeping an eye on how the teeth and jaw are developing. Starting dental visits early means problems like decay or crowding are usually caught before they need major treatment. Beyond preventing disease, these early habits give children a smile they're comfortable with and a routine they carry into adulthood. Parents who want to build good habits at home should ask their dentist for brushing and diet advice suited to their child's age.

title: Internal Bleaching: Treating Discolored Teeth from Within
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Internal bleaching lightens a tooth that has darkened from the inside, often after an injury or a root canal. The dentist works from within the tooth itself, rather than just the surface, to bring the color back closer to its neighbors.
content: Internal bleaching treats a tooth that has darkened from within, which often happens after an injury to the tooth or after a root canal. Unlike whitening toothpaste or over-the-counter strips, which only work on the outer surface, internal bleaching places a whitening agent inside the tooth itself, so the discoloration is treated at its source. Before recommending it, the dentist checks why the tooth darkened and whether the tooth's structure and any previous root canal work can support the procedure. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, patients get an assessment of the tooth first, since not every case of discoloration responds to this treatment, and other options may suit the case better. Once treatment starts, the dentist checks the tooth's color and condition at follow-up visits to confirm the result holds and the tooth stays healthy.

title: Understanding and Managing Pediatric Periodontal Conditions
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Gum disease isn't just an adult problem. Gingivitis and other gum conditions can show up in children too, causing bleeding, swelling, or discomfort, and catching it early makes treatment simpler and gentler.
content: Gingivitis and other gum conditions can affect children as well as adults, sometimes showing up as swollen or bleeding gums, persistent bad breath, or discomfort while eating or brushing. Left unchecked, these problems can affect how a child's teeth and jaw develop. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, the dentist checks a child's gum health at routine visits, using techniques suited to younger patients, and looks for early signs of inflammation before they become bigger problems. Treatment usually starts with a professional cleaning and specific guidance on brushing and flossing, since poor technique is behind most cases of childhood gum irritation. Parents who notice swelling, bleeding, or color changes in their child's gums should bring it up at the next dental visit rather than waiting for it to resolve on its own. Regular check-ups remain the most reliable way to catch gum problems in children early and keep their teeth and gums developing normally.

title: Mucogingival Defects: Diagnosis and Treatment Options
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Gum recession and thinning gum tissue can leave tooth roots exposed, causing sensitivity and making the area harder to keep clean. Catching it early, before more tissue is lost, gives more treatment options and better results.
content: Mucogingival defects cover a range of gum problems, including gum recession, gum tissue that's too thin, or gums that haven't attached properly around a tooth. These issues can cause sensitivity, expose the tooth root, and make it harder to brush and floss effectively around the affected teeth. An experienced dentist in Kolkata can usually spot these problems early, before they progress to more serious gum damage. Treatment depends on what's causing the problem: options include gum grafting to rebuild lost tissue, soft tissue management to reshape and strengthen the gum line, or other periodontal procedures aimed at restoring proper coverage. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic, the dentist examines the gums closely to work out the underlying cause before recommending a treatment plan suited to the case and the patient's comfort. Anyone noticing receding gums, bleeding while brushing, or rising tooth sensitivity should get it checked rather than waiting, since gum tissue is easier to treat before more of it is lost.

title: Aesthetic Crown Lengthening for a Confident Smile
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Crown lengthening reshapes the gum line to show more of the tooth underneath, evening out a gummy smile or preparing a tooth for a crown or filling that needs more surface to work with.
content: Crown lengthening reshapes the gum line to expose more of the tooth structure underneath, which can even out a smile where the gums show more than intended, or prepare a tooth for restorative work such as a crown or filling that needs more surface to work with. It's commonly recommended for what's often called a "gummy" smile, or before dental work that requires extra tooth structure above the gum line. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, the dentist examines the gum and tooth structure first to work out how much reshaping is needed and what result is realistic for that patient. The amount of gum tissue removed and the technique used vary from patient to patient, based on gum thickness and the outcome they're after. Anyone considering crown lengthening should ask their dentist to walk through what the procedure involves and what recovery looks like before deciding to go ahead.

title: Esthetic Gum Procedures: Enhancing Smile and Health
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Esthetic gum procedures cover treatments for uneven gum lines, gummy smiles, gum recession, or dark patches on the gums. Which approach fits best depends on a close look at what's actually causing the issue.
content: Esthetic gum procedures, sometimes called cosmetic gum treatments, address concerns like an uneven gum line, a gummy smile where too much gum shows when smiling, gum recession, or dark pigmentation of the gums. These aren't purely cosmetic issues either; uneven or receding gums can also make teeth harder to keep clean. Working out the right approach starts with a close look at the gums to see what's causing the concern, whether that calls for gum contouring, reshaping, or a more minimally invasive option. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, this assessment comes before any procedure is planned, and patients are walked through what a treatment involves and what result to expect. Anyone considering an esthetic gum procedure should get an accurate diagnosis first, since the right treatment depends entirely on what's causing the gum concern in the first place.

title: Halitosis (Bad Breath): Causes and Professional Management
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Occasional bad breath happens to everyone, but if it doesn't go away with normal brushing and flossing, it's often a sign of gum disease, an infection, or another underlying issue worth checking.
content: Bad breath that comes and goes is usually nothing to worry about, but halitosis that persists despite regular brushing and flossing often points to something else going on, such as gum disease, a dental infection, or another underlying condition. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, the dentist works through the possible causes with an oral exam, checking for gum disease, cavities, or other issues before deciding on treatment. Depending on what's found, treatment might mean a professional cleaning, treating an infection or cavity, or advice on brushing and flossing technique if plaque buildup is the main cause. Diet and daily habits can also play a part, so patients often get specific suggestions for their routine alongside any dental treatment. Anyone dealing with bad breath that doesn't clear up on its own should get it checked, since treating the actual cause works better than masking the smell with mints or mouthwash.

title: Gum Grafting for Receding Gums: A Protective Solution
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Gum grafting covers tooth roots exposed by gum recession, easing sensitivity and slowing further damage. Recession is usually caused by gum disease or overly hard brushing, and a dentist needs to check the extent of it before deciding on treatment.
content:
Gum recession happens when the gum tissue around a tooth wears back and exposes part of the root underneath. Once the root is exposed, teeth often become sensitive to hot, cold, or sweet foods, look longer than before, and are more prone to decay. The most common causes are gum disease, brushing too hard, and gums thinning with age.

Signs to watch for include teeth that appear longer at the gumline, gums that bleed easily, and a sharp reaction when eating or drinking something hot or cold. A dentist examines how much tissue has been lost and how far the recession has progressed before recommending treatment.

Gum grafting involves placing tissue over the exposed root, usually taken from elsewhere in the mouth, to cover it and give the gum a stable edge to reattach to. The procedure reduces sensitivity, protects the root from further wear, and can improve how the gumline looks. Recovery generally takes one to two weeks, during which the dentist's instructions on eating and brushing should be followed closely.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, patients with gum recession are examined to work out the cause before any grafting is planned, since brushing habits or an underlying gum infection often need to be addressed alongside the graft itself. Once the gum has healed, regular brushing, flossing, and check-ups help keep the recession from returning to the same spot.

title: Scaling and Root Planing for Healthy Gums
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Scaling and root planing is deep cleaning that clears plaque and tartar from below the gumline to calm inflammation and stop gums pulling away from the teeth. It's a standard treatment for early and moderate gum disease, usually paired with better brushing and flossing at home.
content:
Scaling and root planing is a deep cleaning procedure used to treat gum disease. When plaque and tartar build up below the gumline, they irritate the gum tissue, causing bleeding, swelling, and eventually infection if left alone. The treatment clears these deposits from the tooth surface and roots, then smooths the root surface so the gum can reattach and heal.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, this is one of the main treatments used for early and moderate gum disease. The dentist examines the gums first to gauge how much tartar has built up and how deep the gum pockets have become, since deeper pockets usually mean a more thorough cleaning is needed. Removing the buildup reduces inflammation, and over time it can also stop teeth from loosening as the gum and bone around them stabilise.

Anyone noticing bleeding gums, bad breath that doesn't go away with brushing, or gum tenderness should get it checked rather than waiting. Scaling and root planing works best combined with good habits at home: brushing twice a day, flossing, and coming back for the recommended follow-up cleanings. Left untreated, gum disease tends to get worse gradually, so catching it at this stage is far easier to manage than later-stage treatment.

title: Gum Recession: Causes, Diagnosis, and Professional Care
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Gum recession exposes tooth roots and raises the risk of sensitivity and decay. Hard brushing and gum disease are the most common causes, and a dentist can catch it early before it progresses further.
content:
Gum recession is when the gum tissue around a tooth pulls back, exposing the root underneath. Once that happens, teeth often become sensitive, more prone to decay near the gumline, and in advanced cases can loosen. Hard brushing is one of the most common causes, along with gum disease, genetics, and hormonal changes that affect gum tissue over time.

Catching recession early makes a real difference. A dentist checks how much gum tissue has receded, looks for signs of gum disease underneath it, and works out what's driving it before suggesting treatment. Depending on the case, that might mean scaling and root planing to clear infection from below the gumline, a gum graft to cover exposed roots, or simply changing how you brush.

At Dr. Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, patients are shown the correct brushing pressure and technique alongside any treatment, since recession caused by hard brushing tends to come back if the habit doesn't change. Left unchecked, recession only gets worse over time, so an early check-up and a change in daily habits usually go a long way toward keeping the rest of the gumline intact.

title: Comprehensive Gum Disease Management in Kolkata
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Gum disease damages the tissue and bone that hold teeth in place, and can lead to tooth loss if it's not treated. Treatment ranges from professional cleaning to deeper procedures depending on how advanced it is, and catching it early makes it far easier to control.
content:
Gum disease, also called periodontal disease, affects the tissue and bone supporting the teeth. In its early stage, gingivitis, gums become red, swollen, and prone to bleeding, but the damage is still reversible with treatment. Left untreated, it can progress to periodontitis, where the infection spreads deeper, teeth loosen, and bone loss becomes permanent.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, treatment depends on how far the disease has progressed. Milder cases usually respond to professional cleaning and better home care. More advanced cases need scaling and root planing to clear infection from below the gumline, and in some cases further periodontal treatment to control the infection and stabilise the gum and bone.

Catching gum disease early matters because the damage it causes to bone and gum tissue generally can't be reversed once it sets in, only managed. Patients are given practical advice on brushing and flossing that actually reaches below the gumline, along with a schedule of follow-up visits to check that the gums are healing and the infection isn't returning. Treated in time, most cases of gum disease can be brought under control without losing any teeth.

title: Scaling and Root Planing for Optimal Gum Health
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Scaling and root planing clears plaque and tartar from beneath the gumline to control gum disease and protect the bone underneath. Paired with good habits at home, it's one of the more effective ways to keep gum problems from coming back.
content:
Scaling and root planing is both a preventive and a treatment procedure for gum health. It involves removing plaque and tartar from the tooth surface and below the gumline, then smoothing the root surface so bacteria have less to cling to and the gum can heal against a clean root.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, the dentist checks gum pocket depth and the extent of tartar buildup before treatment, since deeper pockets need a more thorough clean. The procedure reduces inflammation, helps control periodontal disease, and protects the bone beneath the gums from further damage, which matters because bone loss around the teeth doesn't reverse on its own.

Results depend heavily on what happens after the appointment. Brushing twice a day, flossing, and cutting back on habits like smoking all affect how well the gums hold up afterward, so patients are given specific guidance on technique rather than a generic reminder to brush more. Regular follow-up cleanings, spaced according to how prone someone is to tartar buildup, help keep gum disease from returning. For anyone with bleeding gums, tartar buildup, or gum sensitivity, scaling and root planing is usually the first step before considering any further treatment.

title: Gum Recession: Symptoms, Causes, and Professional Care
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Gum recession exposes tooth roots, causing sensitivity and a higher risk of decay near the gumline. Catching it early, before it progresses, makes it far simpler to treat.
content:
Gum recession is when gum tissue gradually wears back, exposing more of the tooth and its root. It often shows up first as sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet food, discomfort while brushing, or teeth that look longer than they used to. Left unaddressed, the exposed root is more prone to decay and, in some cases, infection.

Brushing too hard, gum disease, teeth grinding, and gum changes that come with age all contribute to recession. At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic, a dentist examines how far the gumline has receded and checks for signs of gum disease before deciding on treatment, since the cause changes what's actually needed. Sometimes it's a change in brushing technique, sometimes deeper cleaning below the gumline, and in more advanced cases, a gum graft to cover the exposed root.

If you notice sensitivity that wasn't there before, visible roots, or gums that look like they're pulling back, it's worth getting checked rather than waiting for it to progress further. Recession doesn't reverse on its own, but catching it early usually means simpler treatment and a better chance of keeping the gumline stable long term.

title: Gum Disease: Prevention, Diagnosis, and Professional Care
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Gum disease shows up as bleeding, swelling, and bad breath before it turns into something more serious. Catching these early signs and cleaning properly at home are what keep it from progressing.
content:
Gum disease affects the gums and the structures that support the teeth. It often starts quietly, with symptoms like bleeding when brushing, swollen or red gums, and bad breath that doesn't clear up on its own. Left untreated, it can progress and eventually lead to tooth loss.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, the first step is usually a check of gum pocket depth and any tartar buildup, so the disease can be caught while it's still at an early, reversible stage. Treatment from there might be a professional cleaning, or scaling and root planing if tartar has built up below the gumline, followed by a plan matched to how advanced the gums have gotten.

What happens at home matters just as much as the treatment itself. Patients are shown, not just told, how to brush and floss in a way that actually reaches below the gumline, since that's usually where gum disease starts. Regular check-ups, roughly every six months, catch problems while they're still gingivitis, before any bone loss sets in, since bone loss is much harder to reverse once it happens. Prevention here is mostly about consistency: good habits at home and not skipping the follow-up visits.

title: TMJ Pain Management: Relief for Jaw Discomfort
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: TMJ disorders can cause jaw pain, clicking, headaches, and trouble chewing. Treatment starts with figuring out the actual cause, then may involve a bite check, jaw exercises, or a custom appliance to ease the strain.
content:
Jaw pain, a clicking sound when opening the mouth, headaches, and difficulty chewing can all point to a problem with the temporomandibular joint, the joint connecting the jaw to the skull. Left unaddressed, TMJ problems can interfere with eating, sleep, and everyday comfort.

At Dr Maria's Multispeciality Dental Clinic in Kolkata, TMJ pain is worked through by first finding what's actually causing the strain on the joint, since jaw pain can come from several different sources and the right treatment depends on which one applies. That might mean checking whether the bite is misaligned, looking at clenching or grinding habits, and, where needed, fitting a custom appliance to keep the jaw from overworking during sleep. Gentle jaw exercises are also used in some cases to improve movement and ease stiffness.

Getting an accurate diagnosis matters more than it might seem, since TMJ symptoms overlap with other causes of jaw and facial pain, and treating the wrong one won't help. Left untreated for too long, TMJ problems tend to get stiffer and more painful rather than better on their own. Anyone with jaw pain that isn't going away, clicking, or trouble opening their mouth fully should get it looked at before it progresses further.

title: Temporomandibular Joint Disorder: Maintaining Jaw Function
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: TMJ disorder affects the jaw joint and the muscles around it, causing pain, stiffness, and trouble chewing, sometimes along with clicking or a jaw that locks. Catching it early makes it far easier to manage. Treatment usually starts with simple, non-invasive options like exercises or a custom bite appliance, backed up by daily habits that protect the jaw over the long run.
content:
The temporomandibular joint connects the jaw to the skull, and when it or the surrounding muscles are under strain, the result is often pain, general discomfort, and difficulty chewing. Some people also notice clicking, popping, or the jaw locking briefly when they open or close their mouth.

TMJ problems tend to become harder to manage the longer they go unaddressed, so an early assessment is worth getting. At Dr. Maria's Multi-Speciality Dental Clinic in Newtown, Kolkata, the dentist checks how the jaw moves and looks into what's behind the discomfort before suggesting a plan, since the right treatment depends on the specific cause.

Most cases start with the least invasive options available: exercises to ease muscle tension, small adjustments to how the teeth meet, or a custom appliance that takes pressure off the joint. Patients also get practical advice on daily habits worth changing, since small adjustments to how the jaw is used day to day make a real difference to how well the treatment holds up.

Managed early, TMJ disorder is usually kept under control without more invasive procedures, and most people see their pain ease and normal jaw movement return within a reasonable stretch of time.

title: Surgical Management of Oral Fibromas
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: An oral fibroma is a harmless lump that can still get in the way of chewing or feel uncomfortable if it's left alone. Removing it is a quick, straightforward procedure with a short recovery. Afterward, simple hygiene steps and addressing whatever caused the irritation in the first place keep a new one from forming.
content:
An oral fibroma is a firm, non-cancerous growth that can form on the gums, cheeks, or tongue, usually from ongoing irritation, such as biting the cheek repeatedly or rubbing against a rough tooth or denture. It isn't dangerous, but it can make chewing awkward or simply be an annoying thing to have in your mouth.

Once a growth is causing irritation or continues to enlarge, surgical removal is generally the simplest fix. At Dr. Maria's Multi-Speciality Dental Clinic in Newtown, Kolkata, the procedure is done under local anaesthesia and takes only a short time, with a stitch or two placed if needed to help the area heal cleanly. Most patients are back to normal within a few days.

After removal, the dentist goes over basic aftercare: keeping the area clean, steering clear of hard or spicy food for a short while, and watching for swelling. Just as important is dealing with whatever caused the irritation in the first place, whether that's a sharp tooth edge or a poorly fitting denture, since that's what actually stops the fibroma from returning.

A lump that isn't going away on its own is worth having checked rather than waiting out. Getting it looked at early makes for a straightforward diagnosis and an easier removal.

title: Effective Management of Oral Infections
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Oral infections can be as minor as gum irritation or as serious as an abscess putting a tooth at risk. Finding the actual cause, rather than just treating symptoms, is what keeps a small problem from becoming a bigger one. Good daily hygiene and a follow-up visit or two go a long way toward stopping infections from coming back.
content:
Not every oral infection looks the same. Some show up as mild gum redness that clears with better brushing, while others, like an abscessed tooth or a deeper gum infection, bring swelling, throbbing pain, and can affect neighbouring teeth if left alone.

Working out which is which starts with a proper look at what's going on. At Dr. Maria's Multi-Speciality Dental Clinic in Newtown, Kolkata, the dentist examines the affected area, may take an X-ray to see how far things have spread, and asks about symptoms like pain, swelling, or an unpleasant taste before deciding on treatment, whether that's a deep cleaning, antibiotics, drainage, or root canal therapy.

Once the immediate infection is under control, the next task is stopping it from happening again. That mostly comes down to brushing and flossing properly, treating cavities or gum disease before they progress, and keeping up with regular check-ups so small issues get caught early.

Waiting out an oral infection rarely helps and can let it spread further. Coming in sooner and following through on the treatment plan is what keeps these problems from turning into something more serious.

title: Managing a Fractured Tooth: Professional Dental Care
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: A fractured tooth, whether from an accident, a hard bite, or decay that's weakened it from within, usually brings sudden sensitivity or sharp pain. Treatment depends on how deep the crack runs, from simple bonding to a crown or a root canal. Getting it checked quickly limits the damage and keeps the tooth from getting worse.
content:
Teeth crack for a range of reasons: a fall or a blow to the face, biting down on something hard like ice or a bone, or a cavity that has weakened the tooth from the inside. The result is usually sudden sensitivity to hot or cold, or sharp pain when chewing.

Because a crack can let bacteria in and lead to infection if it's ignored, it's worth getting checked soon rather than waiting to see if it settles. At Dr. Maria's Multi-Speciality Dental Clinic in Newtown, Kolkata, the first step is an exam and an X-ray to see how deep the fracture runs and whether it has reached the nerve.

Treatment follows from what that exam shows. A minor chip can often be fixed with bonding in a single visit. A larger fracture might need a crown to hold the tooth together, and if the crack has reached the nerve, a root canal usually comes first, before the tooth is capped. When a tooth can't be saved, extraction followed by a bridge or implant restores the bite.

Afterward, the dentist usually points out habits worth changing, like chewing ice, using teeth to open packaging, or skipping a mouthguard during sports, since these are common causes of repeat fractures. Along with regular brushing and check-ups, avoiding those habits is the best way to protect a repaired tooth going forward.

title: Mucogingival Surgery: Restoring Gum Health and Aesthetics
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Mucogingival surgery treats gum recession and thin gum tissue that leaves tooth roots exposed. Beyond how it looks, covering the roots back up cuts down on sensitivity and decay risk. Whether the fix is a tissue graft or reshaping depends on the individual case, and results hold up best with good hygiene and regular follow-up.
content:
When gums pull back from the teeth, whether from brushing too hard, gum disease, or the shape of someone's bite, the exposed root underneath becomes more prone to sensitivity and decay, and the gumline can start to look uneven. Mucogingival surgery corrects this by adding or reshaping gum tissue where it has thinned or gone missing.

The right approach depends on how much recession there is and where it's happening. Some cases call for a tissue graft, where healthy gum tissue, often taken from the roof of the mouth, is placed over the exposed root. Others need only reshaping of the existing tissue to even out the gumline. The dentist decides which method fits after checking the extent of the recession and the condition of the surrounding gum and bone.

At Dr. Maria's Multi-Speciality Dental Clinic in Newtown, Kolkata, patients go through a pre-surgical assessment and a clear explanation of the procedure before going ahead, along with specific instructions for the days after surgery to support clean healing.

The results tend to hold up well over time, but only with upkeep: gentle brushing technique and regular dental visits to catch any new recession early. Anyone noticing gum recession or increased sensitivity near the gumline should have a dentist take a look to see whether this procedure would help.

title: Porcelain Veneers: A Natural-Looking Smile Enhancement
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Porcelain veneers are thin shells bonded to the front of teeth to cover stains, chips, gaps, or uneven edges that whitening alone can't fix. Fitting them well takes careful planning and only a small amount of tooth reshaping so they sit securely and match the surrounding teeth. With decent hygiene and regular check-ups, they hold up for years.
content:
A veneer is a thin layer of porcelain bonded over the visible front of a tooth, used to cover staining, small chips, gaps, or shapes that look uneven. Because porcelain takes on a tooth-like colour and sheen, a well-made veneer is hard to pick out from a natural tooth.

They tend to come up as an option once whitening or simple reshaping isn't enough to get the result someone wants. Fitting them properly takes some preparation: a small amount of enamel is removed from the front of the tooth so the veneer sits flush rather than bulky, and each one is shaped and shaded to match its neighbours.

At Dr. Maria's Multi-Speciality Dental Clinic in Newtown, Kolkata, the process starts with checking the health of the teeth and gums to see whether veneers are a good fit, followed by planning around shade, shape, and how many teeth are involved.

Veneers aren't indestructible, so avoiding habits like biting nails or chewing on pens helps them last, and regular brushing, flossing, and check-ups keep both the veneers and the teeth underneath in good shape for years. Anyone thinking about fixing chips, gaps, or discoloration this way can start with a straightforward conversation with a dentist about whether veneers suit their teeth.

title: Root Canal Treatment: Saving Damaged Teeth
author: Dr Maria's Multi-speciality Dental Clinic
subtitle: Root canal treatment removes infected pulp from inside a tooth so it can be saved instead of pulled. It's usually needed when deep decay, a crack, or a failed filling lets bacteria reach the nerve. Digital X-rays and rotary instruments make the procedure quicker and more comfortable than its reputation suggests, and a filling or crown afterward brings the tooth back to full strength.
content:
A root canal becomes necessary when the pulp, the soft tissue inside a tooth, gets infected or inflamed. This can happen from a deep cavity left untreated, a crack that lets bacteria in, a filling that has failed, or an injury to the tooth. Left alone, the infection causes swelling and often severe pain, and can eventually cost you the tooth.

The procedure removes the infected pulp, then cleans and shapes the canals inside the root before sealing them to keep bacteria out. Once that's done, the tooth needs a filling or a crown on top to restore its strength and appearance, since a tooth without its pulp becomes more brittle over time.

At Dr. Maria's Multi-Speciality Dental Clinic in Newtown, Kolkata, root canals are done using digital X-rays and rotary instruments, which speed up the cleaning and shaping of the canals and make for a smoother, more comfortable procedure than the old manual approach. Most patients find it far more manageable than they expected going in.

A tooth that's had a root canal and been properly capped can last for decades, sometimes a lifetime, as long as it's kept clean and checked at regular visits like any other tooth.
